chosen_mechanism: GS2, four statically indexed AF banks ci&3, wait_group2, previous X release atci1; same one576-threadCTA, FT64,3joined TMA slots, all packing/traffic/math unchanged
findings: Four banks divide8groups per stage; bankq&3 was last used byq-4, which preceding wait2 has retired. At a stage boundary oldgroups6/7 usebanks2/3, leavingbank0 safe.
After first group of next stage, oldgroup7 may still read previousX. After second group ci1 wait2, all previous-stage groups retired. Only then may each warp return previousX credit.

All four warpgroups retain existing16 total X-release arrivals. Three X slots permit successorstageq+1 to be issued before producer needsqslot forq+3, so delayedrelease does not create ring dependency cycle.
NTT1 accumulator parity must stayci&1 independently of AFbankci&3; first mma0 guards and segment-end wait0/add are unchanged.

FCI3 flush uses preceding drained segment, not current AF/d. Withwait2 it runs withtwo live currentgroups and may increase compiler pressure; source/math correctness does not establish no serialization.
Negative models detect two-bank/wait2 overwrite, threebank reset-at-stage overwrite, and previousX release atci0.

GS4 earlier used4k16/group onlyforNTT1 and changed accumulation partition; newproposal keeps2k16/group and exactparent trace. Earlier96regs/local0 inGS4 does not prove resource fit for broadnewwideNTT paths.
No prior MAIN WGS af3/af4+wait2 implementation found in retained candidates, researchrecords and public_scout files searched; attentionrolePIPE kernels are distinct workloads.
NCU stall_wait8.11/9.58%, issue~59.4%, DRAM~75% are descriptive aggregate counters without source-PC attribution; they provide neither measured queue-depth bottleneck nor gain bound.
